listing.name: Chris Sawyer's Locomotion / OpenLoco (OpenLoco)
listing.summary: Play Chris Sawyer’s Locomotion with OpenLoco on Windows x64, Linux x64 or Apple Silicon Mac. Bring your own Locomotion data.

steps.title: Start the game
steps.instruction: On first Play, OpenLoco detects your installed Chris Sawyer’s Locomotion files or asks you to select the original folder containing Data/g1.DAT. The official portable engine needs no separate build or installer.

references.title: Set up OpenLoco on Linux
references.instruction: For a separately prepared copy, use the official x86-64 AppImage with FUSE support. The reviewed player needs glibc 2.28 or newer. Make it executable and run it directly to select your installed Locomotion directory containing Data/g1.DAT. Preserve the whole profile under ~/.config/OpenLoco or the actual XDG_CONFIG_HOME location. Keep separately selected saves, landscapes, custom objects and original-game folders.

references.title: Set up OpenLoco on Apple Silicon
references.instruction: For a separately prepared copy, use the upstream macos-arm64 ZIP on macOS 15 or newer. If downloading through Portcove, clear “Extract the archive after downloading”. Extract it with the system archive tool and keep the entire OpenLoco.app bundle. Upstream describes this build as unsigned and unnotarized. Follow its Mac instructions if Gatekeeper blocks it. Start it directly, select the Locomotion directory containing Data/g1.DAT and preserve ~/Library/Application Support/OpenLoco and custom locations. You manage this external copy and its updates.

presentation.manual_preparation: On first Play, select your original Locomotion installation containing Data/g1.DAT. Keep it outside the managed runtime. Linux x64 uses the official AppImage with FUSE support and glibc 2.28 or newer. The Apple Silicon bundle requires macOS 15 or newer. Keep the full engine package together. Back up your external OpenLoco profile separately. On Windows it normally lives under AppData. On Linux it lives under XDG_CONFIG_HOME or the account home’s .config directory. On Mac it lives under Library/Application Support in the account home. Use a separately prepared copy for custom or relative save and landscape locations. Keep your player files and originals outside the library. Portcove replaces its engine and leaves those player files in place.
